messages:
jamie: Heads-up — starting a 'quiet start' bring-up for the Northstar satellite cluster (private/VPC, air-gapped). Goal: minimal traffic churn, validate GPU provisioning, networking, and hand off to delivery next week. Sharing a short runbook and want quick ops eyes.

jamie: Runbook (summary):
  1) Prepare air-gapped image sync (registry -> local mirror).
  2) Seed control-plane nodes and kubelet configs (MTU=9000).
  3) Provision GPU nodepool (2x A100 per node for initial capacity).
  4) Validate NVLINK + MIG partitions, run basic perf smoke.
  5) Network sanity: BGP neighbors, route leak tests, egress NAT, and DNS forwarding.
  6) Cost & sizing check + labels/tags for billing + handoff doc.

jamie: Attaching quick commands below — run them from the on-prem bastion after image sync:

```
# mirror images (run on mirror host)
rsync -avz --progress /mnt/registry-images/ northstar-mirror:/var/lib/registry/
# on bastion - kubelet check
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | egrep "Capacity|Allocatable|nvidia"
```

rachel: Nice. For step 1, confirm the mirror will have the same repo paths as our hosted registry (so images can be pulled unchanged). Who is owning the rsync window?

jamie: I'll own the rsync. Plan is to window it 02:00-04:00 UTC to avoid customer churn. Mirror path is identical to staging so `imagePullSecrets` shouldn't change.

oncall-bot: [automated] mirror-sync started at 2026-03-16T02:05:12Z (expected duration ~40m).

omar: Quick note — last time we had MTU mismatch on the south-facing router; caused large packet drops for CUDA transfers. Confirm MTU=9000 on all overlay and host interfaces, and check iptables conntrack settings for high concurrent streams.

jamie: Good call. We'll run an MTU probe post-provision: `ping -M do -s 8972 <peer>` and `ethtool -k eth0`.

sree: For air-gapped customers, also ensure our internal cert CNs match the hostnames they expect. We should pre-generate node certs and drop them via the seed step to avoid kubelet bootstrap timing issues. Add this to runbook: generate certs + push via `scp` with checksum.

jamie: Added. Also planning to run a quick GPU smoke after kubelet ready:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv
# basic perf test
python -c "import time; print('warmup'); time.sleep(0.2)"
```

rachel: On capacity — starting with 4 nodes (8x A100 total) keeps us under the committed baseline for the first month if we set autoscale min=2, max=8. delivery-ops, OK from a contract/cost perspective?

delivery-ops: budget ack — go ahead with 4 nodes as initial. Two asks: tag nodes with `env:northstar` + `billing:project-northstar`; and prefer reserved on the monthly plan for 50% of the pool after the first month to reduce unit costs.

omar: When we provision the nodepool, run this to validate NVLINK and ensure MIG profiles are correct:
```
nvidia-smi nvlink --status
nvidia-smi mig -l
```
Also check `dmesg | grep NVRM` for driver errors.

jamie: Noted. Ops checklist (for handoff):
  - [ ] mirror verified and images accessible from worker nodes
  - [ ] all nodes Ready in kube (kubectl get nodes shows Ready)
  - [ ] GPU health checks pass (nvidia-smi + nvlink)
  - [ ] kernel/dmesg free of NVRM errors for 30m
  - [ ] MTU/probing passed across AZs and VPC peerings
  - [ ] BGP neighbors established and route test (traceroute) ok
  - [ ] billing tags applied and cost estimate doc uploaded to shared drive
  - [ ] runbook + minimal recovery playbook pushed to customer repo

sree: Add: smoke-run for inference binary to assert p50 latency under 120ms for 8-token prompt at cold start. If we fail, fallback to smaller batch size and log the config.

jamie: Will run smoke-run and capture traces. Also putting a temp route-limiter in place to avoid disk pressure from image pulls: `ip route blackhole 0.0.0.0/0 metric 100` while mirror finalizes.

rachel: Heads-up: during Sea2 bring-up we had a routing issue because the customer's firewall NAT-ed source IPs; our kube-probes failed (source mismatch). Recommend we test readiness probes from a jump pod using hostNetwork to reproduce.

omar: +1. Also watch for iptables rules leftover from prior installs — `iptables -S` on the node prior to kubelet start. We should ensure to disable nftables wrappers if present.

oncall-bot: [automated] initial health-check report (2118002000): 4 control-plane seeds reachable, mirror checksums match (sha256), kubelet versions consistent across nodes. See logs: https://internal.ops/reports/northstar/2118002000

delivery-ops: Cost note — with initial 4 node baseline and expected 40% utilization, projected monthly spend ~ $26k before reserved discounts. We'll need to revisit in 2 weeks.

rachel: For handoff: if all checks green, propose a soft-handoff on 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC. Delivery ops will take over incident duties and maintain the runbook.

jamie: Sounds good. I'll run the smoke tests now and post results. Leaving a pinned checklist in the channel once core items pass.

omar: Quick troubleshooting tip (if you hit OOM on kubelet): check `kube-reserved` settings in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` and ensure `systemReserved` accounts for the GPU driver memory.

jamie: Update — mirror finished, rsync exit 0. Starting node boot at 02:45 UTC.

oncall-bot: [automated] node-bootstrap event 2118003000: 4/4 nodes joined, kube-system pods initializing.

jamie: GPU smoke summary (2118003500): all GPUs visible, nvlink ok, no NVRM in dmesg for 45m. Basic inference smoke p50=98ms on one-shot test. Uploading perf logs to the runbook.

rachel: Great. tagging + cost doc uploaded. I’ll schedule the handoff meeting and send invites.

jamie: Handoff scheduled. If anyone sees odd IO patterns overnight please ping me. Otherwise we can move to delivery-ops ownership tomorrow. :thumbsup:

delivery-ops: Received — will take over monitoring and costs. Thanks team. :shipit:
